CRITICAL UX FAILURE & EXECUTIVE ACTION REQUIRED: Restoring Fundamental Watch Behavior via Adaptive Power

Dear Samsung Electronics Executive Leadership (Product Strategy, UX Architecture, Software Engineering, and Wearable Platform Teams),

I would like to raise a critical user experience issue affecting the Galaxy Watch series.

This is not a feature request.

This is a fundamental usability issue affecting the core purpose of a watch.

Core Problem: The Removal of Raise to Wake

A watch, regardless of how advanced its technology may be, exists primarily for one essential purpose:

It must show the time immediately when the user looks at it.

For decades, the natural interaction between a person and a watch has remained unchanged. The user raises their wrist, glances at the watch, and instantly sees the time.

Galaxy Watch successfully modernized this behavior through Raise to Wake.

This feature is not merely a convenience. It is one of the foundational interactions of the entire Galaxy Watch experience.

The watch detects intentional wrist movement and immediately presents information without requiring any additional action.

This behavior is what makes a smartwatch feel like a watch.

Currently, when Power Saving Mode is enabled, Raise to Wake becomes unavailable.

This creates a contradiction.

Power Saving Mode is designed for situations where battery life becomes most valuable. Ironically, these are also the moments when users need the fastest and most efficient access to the time.

Instead of simply raising their wrist, users must touch the display or press a button.

At that moment, the device no longer behaves like a watch.

It behaves like a powered-down electronic device requiring manual activation.

Why This Creates UX Friction

Checking the time is one of the most frequent interactions performed on any watch.

Users may perform this action dozens or even hundreds of times per day.

Every additional tap, button press, or interaction introduces friction into what should be an effortless experience.

The issue becomes particularly noticeable during:

• Walking
• Driving
• Exercising
• Carrying objects
• Outdoor activities
• Professional work environments

In these situations, Raise to Wake is not a luxury feature.

It is the expected behavior of a watch.

The Contradiction of Power Saving Mode

Power Saving Mode should reduce non-essential power consumption.

However, Raise to Wake is not a non-essential function.

It is the mechanism through which the watch fulfills its primary purpose.

Reducing animations, background activity, refresh rates, sensor frequency, health monitoring intervals, and other power-intensive processes is understandable.

Removing immediate access to the time is not.

A watch that cannot conveniently show the time when the user raises their wrist undermines the fundamental reason the product is worn in the first place.

Recommended Solution: Adaptive Power Mode

Samsung could implement an Adaptive Power approach where:

• Raise to Wake remains available
• Display-on duration is shortened
• Animations are simplified
• Refresh rates are reduced
• Background activity is further optimized
• Non-critical functions remain restricted

This would preserve battery life while maintaining the fundamental identity of the product.

Strategic Business Impact

This change would:

• Improve daily usability
• Reduce user frustration
• Increase customer satisfaction
• Strengthen ecosystem loyalty
• Improve perceived software intelligence
• Reinforce Samsung's reputation for thoughtful UX design

Most importantly, it would preserve the defining interaction that makes Galaxy Watch feel like a watch.

Conclusion

Power Saving Mode should never remove the most essential interaction of a watch.

A user should always be able to raise their wrist and immediately see the time.

Raise to Wake is not a premium feature.

It is not an optional convenience.

It is one of the core foundations of the Galaxy Watch experience.

I respectfully ask Samsung's Product, UX, and Engineering teams to review this behavior and consider restoring Raise to Wake functionality within Power Saving Mode through an adaptive implementation.

Thank you for your time, consideration, and continued commitment to improving the Galaxy Watch platform
